# VidaExtra — Spanish retrospective

- Original source: [Retroanálisis de Robin Hood: La Leyenda de Sherwood, el noble Commandos medieval](https://www.vidaextra.com/analisis/robin-hood-leyenda-sherwood-analisis-review-precio-experiencia-juego-para-pc)

- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (commercial retrospective, not transcribed)

Jarkendia praises the medieval setting, attractive towns, and complementary character abilities. The review discusses learning mouse-drawn sword attacks, managing stamina, and finding alternate routes such as rooftops.

Its strongest criticism is repeated scenery, especially forest areas, alongside limited mission variety and combat controls that need refinement. The author still regards the game fondly and would welcome a remaster. This offers a useful counterpoint to reviews that emphasize mission variety: discovering routes remains rewarding here, but repeated locations weaken the overall campaign experience.

Spanish commercial retrospective, not transcribed.

Content, in order:

- Intro: Pyro Studios' first Commandos (1998) set a benchmark for isometric action-strategy; several imitators followed without the same impact. Spellbound Entertainment tried hardest, launching two series in that style: Desperados (with two more instalments "to forget", and a return under THQ Nordic expected in 2020) and Robin Hood: La Leyenda de Sherwood, which had no sequel but is remembered fondly.
- Section "Volverá antes de que esta flecha toque el suelo": the Pyro formula had little competition until Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun (Mimimi) surpassed it almost 20 years later. Robin Hood was released four years after Commandos, adopted the formula, but changed how enemies are faced once stealth fails: sword duels rather than simply clicking on the enemy.
- Combat: lines drawn with the mouse produce direct cuts, lateral cuts, or a powerful spin that consumes more stamina and can leave the character exhausted. It took time to learn which techniques suit which opponent, and several enemies at once made survival hard.
- Allies had unique abilities and different combat skill. Robin was best with the bow; aiming resembled the Commandos sniper except for the arrows' arcing trajectory. Sometimes stealth and knocking out an unalerted enemy was better. Criticism: hiding spots were "quite limited" apart from house interiors, a few of which showed their hidden part, with some confusion caused by background sections.
- Section "Robin Hood, la leyenda que no te decía okidoki": the adventure was harsher because of brawls in later stages and how hard stealth was, even using enemy warnings or the single-enemy vision view from the top-right tab. Biggest flaw: "incomprehensible recycling of scenery", repeated to an exaggerated degree around Sherwood.
- Missions varied, but none was truly memorable because the band's abilities were not fully exploited. Discovering new routes was rewarding; Robin was very agile and could jump across rooftops.
- Team play was encouraged by Robin's limits: he could not finish off a knocked-out enemy on the ground; others did the dirty work, both killing and carrying the body elsewhere. Beggars could be paid coins for information.
- Anecdote: the CGI videos have aged badly and show Robin firing an arrow so far it would not fall for weeks until the king's return.
- Section "¿Ha aguantado bien el paso del tiempo?": yes, but replaying today shows the gameplay needs polish and that the lack of scenery and mission variety has taken its toll; the author would be very glad of a remaster given how many genre classics are returning.

Lo mejor: a Commandos set in Sherwood; good variety of abilities among the heroes; very striking city scenarios. Lo peor: recycles scenery too much; really little mission variety; combat control could be better.
